title: Validations help users; constraints protect rows
outcome: Choose the right layer for uniqueness and evolve a schema safely.

exercises.title: Find and fix the bug
exercises.prompt: A unique validation passes in tests but duplicates appear during imports. Repair the rule and identify a migration risk.

exercises.title: Change one condition
exercises.prompt: You must add a required status to a table with old rows. Write a staged plan rather than one optimistic add_column call.

trace.title: Input validation
trace.detail: A model validation gives readable feedback before a save. A database constraint protects stored data even when two requests race or a different code path writes the table. Use both when the rule matters.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
Two transactions can both pass a uniqueness validator before either inserts. The unique index makes only one conflicting insert succeed. The losing code must handle the database error and return a useful result.

For a rename, use expand → backfill → switch reads/writes → remove old data later. Verify both versions work during deployment. Test the migration on a disposable database with old-shaped data.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: update_all bypasses model callbacks and validations. That can be useful for a deliberate batch update, but database constraints still apply. A rollback that drops a filled column destroys values.
